{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Jane Piore Gilman''' (born 1945)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/000000011084853X ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-11-27.</ref> is an American [[mathematician]], a distinguished professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]].<ref name="cv">[http://andromeda.rutgers.edu/~gilman/CV3-21-13.pdf Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130409134320/http://andromeda.rutgers.edu/~gilman/CV3-21-13.pdf |date=2013-04-09 }}, February 8, 2013, retrieved 2014-06-14.</ref> Her research concerns [[topology]] and [[group theory]].

==Education and career==
Gilman is one of three children of physicist [[Emanuel R. Piore]].<ref>{{citation|title=Emanuel Piore, 91, Leader And Researcher at I.B.M.|journal=[[New York Times]]|first=Wolfgang|last=Saxon|date=May 12, 2000|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/05/12/us/emanuel-piore-91-leader-and-researcher-at-ibm.html}}.</ref> She did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Chicago]], graduating in 1965,<ref name="cv"/> and received her Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]] in 1971. Her thesis, supervised by [[Lipman Bers]], was entitled ''Relative Modular Groups in Teichmüller Spaces''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Jane Piore Gilman|id=20002}}</ref> She worked for a year as an instructor at [[Stony Brook University]] before joining Rutgers in 1972.<ref name="cv"/>

==Books==
Gilman is the author of a monograph on the problem of testing whether pairs of elements of [[Projective linear group|PSL(2,'''R''')]] (the group of orientation-preserving [[isometry|isometries]] of the [[hyperbolic plane]]) generate a [[Fuchsian group]] (a [[discrete group|discrete subgroup]] of PSL(2,'''R''')). It is ''Two-generator Discrete Subgroups of ''PSL(2, '''R''') (Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society 117, 1995).<ref>Review of ''Two-generator Discrete Subgroups of ''PSL(2, '''R''') by C. Maclachlan (1997), {{MR|1290281}}.</ref> With [[Irwin Kra]] and [[Rubí Rodríguez|Rubí E. Rodríguez]] she is the co-author of a graduate-level textbook on [[complex analysis]], ''Complex Analysis: In the Spirit of Lipman Bers'' ([[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]] 245, Springer, 2007; 2nd ed., 2013).<ref>Review of ''Complex Analysis: In the Spirit of Lipman Bers'' (2nd ed.) by Leonid V. Kovalev, {{MR|2986247}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2014, she was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to topology and group theory, and for service to her department and the larger community."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref>
